preamble: Excrescence of [d]: a transitional voiced stop arises between a nasal or /l/ and a following liquid (/nr/ > /ndr/, /nl/ > /ndl/, /lr/ > /ldr/). The velum closes before the tongue releases, so a brief oral stop forms. It appears independently in English, Gallo-Romance and Catalan, and Ancient Greek.

examples.note: Excrescent d between n and r (compare Dutch donder).
d inserted in the nl cluster.
After the post-tonic vowel was lost, the new n'r cluster got an excrescent d.
Wiktionary explicitly gives tendre as an epenthetic form of older tenre.
Where the stem vowel is lost (genitive ἀνδρός, dative ἀνδρί), δ appears between ν and ρ; the nominative is ἀνήρ.
